business_process: Reservoir and spillway gate operations, including flood passage
description: Set the 20 spillway gates to follow each reservoir operating plan, pass floods, and keep reservoirs within license limits; done from the ROC, the plant HMIs, or local panels
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Life safety: a wrong gate opening sends a surge toward Blackwater Bend (city of about 38,000 within 2 to 9 miles), Cedar Shoals, or Pine Hollow; loss of gate control in a flood could overtop a dam. Local control needs an operator at each panel: 8 at BWB, 5 at CDS, 4 at PNH, 3 at SGR. MTD is how long the company can staff all 20 panels safely (about 4 hours before relief crews are needed). RPO covers gate position and reservoir history in the historian
manual_workaround: Operators run gates from the 20 local panels with radio contact to the ROC shift supervisor; hoists on standby generators; reservoir read from staff gauges; roving operator plus call-out crew at Sawgrass Run
dependent_third_parties: SCADA platform vendor (integrator); upstream and downstream dam owners (flow coordination)
dependent_people_or_facilities: ROC shift (6 operators); plant operators at 4 projects; call-out list of 22 qualified gate operators; 4 spillways; standby generators
quantified_operational_impact: 20 gates at 4 dams; all-local operation needs 20 people on site at once, about 3 times normal staffing at CDS, PNH, and SGR
quantified_regulatory_impact: Gate misoperation and security incidents are conditions affecting project safety (18 CFR 12.3(b)(4)(ii), (xi)); 12.10 report preferably within 72 hours; possible EAP activation
public_safety_impact: Severe: uncontrolled release or overtopping; the 4 EAP inundation zones hold about 45,600 people
ferc_security_plan_linkage: Rev. 3A 7.4.1 Internal Emergency Response (BWB, CDS, PNH); 7.4.2 Rapid Recovery (BWB); Table 9.3a restoration and recovery; Form 3 Q16 and Q20

business_process: Dam safety monitoring and EAP early warning
description: Read 410 instruments and 9 upstream gauges against trigger points; detect developing failure modes; sound the 23 downstream sirens and make EAP notifications
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Life safety and 18 CFR 12.10 (unusual instrument readings are reportable, 12.3(b)(4)(viii)). Data loggers buffer 30 days, so little data is lost, but trend review stops. Sirens have local activation at each pole. 8 hours is the longest gap the Chief Dam Safety Engineer accepts before manual readings must cover every critical instrument
manual_workaround: Manual readings of the 86 critical instruments every 4 hours by dam safety technicians; siren activation from local poles; EAP phone tree from printed contact lists
dependent_third_parties: Instrumentation hardware vendor; cellular carrier (river gauges); county emergency management in 3 counties
dependent_people_or_facilities: 64 dam safety staff; ROC shift; siren maintenance contractor
quantified_operational_impact: 86 critical instruments need about 30 technician-hours per 4-hour reading cycle across 4 dams
quantified_regulatory_impact: 12.10 reporting of unusual readings; EAP notification duties (12.20 to 12.25)
public_safety_impact: Severe: a missed warning delays evacuation of an inundation zone
ferc_security_plan_linkage: Rev. 3A 3.2 (trigger points for action from critical instrumentation); 7.4.1; Table 9.3a restoration and recovery

business_process: Generation and unit control at Blackwater Bend and Cedar Shoals (BES)
description: Start, load, and stop the 6 BES units to the BA/TOP schedule from the ROC; protect the units; follow dispatch instructions
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $301,600 of generation revenue per day at average output (BWB $203,400; CDS $98,200). Units can run from local plant HMIs at BWB (staffed 24x7) and CDS (day shift plus call-out) at reduced flexibility. GOP duties to follow BA/TOP instructions continue. Water not used for generation passes through the spillway, which BP-01 must manage
manual_workaround: Local unit control from plant HMIs and unit panels; BWB control room staffed 24x7; CDS call-out crew; schedule by phone with the BA/TOP
dependent_third_parties: Governor and excitation OEM (BWB, CDS); SCADA platform vendor; BA/TOP (offtaker utility)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Plant operators; controls engineering on call; BWB and CDS powerhouses
quantified_operational_impact: About 264 MW; local control keeps about half of normal output during the first 12 hours
quantified_regulatory_impact: NERC GOP obligations continue (follow BA/TOP instructions); EOP-004-4 report if damage or a physical threat is involved; PPA deviation charges
public_safety_impact: Moderate: water hammer or overspeed risk if unit controls are misoperated; worker safety during manual operation
ferc_security_plan_linkage: Rev. 3A 7.4.2 Rapid Recovery (generation at BWB); Table 9.1c (BWB generation Operational on capacity)

business_process: Generation and unit control at Pine Hollow and Sawgrass Run
description: Run the 6 small units at PNH (day shift) and SGR (unstaffed) from the ROC; offtaker is an electric cooperative
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $49,100 of generation revenue per day (PNH $31,600; SGR $17,500). SGR is unstaffed, so loss of ROC control means sending the roving operator; PNH governors and SGR turbine controls are serviced only by their OEMs
manual_workaround: PNH local HMI on day shift; SGR units shut down and spill, with the roving operator on site
dependent_third_parties: Governor OEM (PNH); turbine controls OEM (SGR); electric cooperative
dependent_people_or_facilities: PNH operators; roving operator; PNH and SGR powerhouses
quantified_operational_impact: 36 MW; SGR output stops when ROC control is lost
quantified_regulatory_impact: Cooperative contract notice; 12.10 if a gate or unit misoperates
public_safety_impact: Moderate: unstaffed site; a misoperated unit at SGR could change tailwater for anglers below the dam
ferc_security_plan_linkage: Section 9 interconnection: SGR (Group 3) is interconnected to the ROC and held to the same level (Rev. 3A 9.1.1.2 note)

business_process: ROC supervision and real-time data exchange with the BA/TOP (ICCP)
description: Monitor and control all 4 projects from one Control Center; exchange real-time data with the BA/TOP control center over the ICCP link; fail over to the backup ROC at Cedar Shoals
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The ROC is a GOP Control Center. The BA/TOP needs real-time data from BWB and CDS; CIP-012-2 R1 requires methods for loss of the link and its recovery. Failover to the backup ROC takes about 90 minutes (staff travel to CDS). 4 hours is the time the BA/TOP accepts on phone updates before it re-dispatches
manual_workaround: Fail over to the backup ROC at Cedar Shoals; voice updates to the BA/TOP every 30 minutes; plant control rooms take local control
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-05; SYS-09 (MFA for jump hosts)
dependent_third_parties: BA/TOP (offtaker utility); leased circuit carrier for ICCP; SCADA platform vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: 36 ROC staff; backup ROC at CDS; ROC Manager
quantified_operational_impact: One ROC supervises 300 MW and 20 gates plus 6 RMOS client projects
quantified_regulatory_impact: CIP-012-2 R1 Parts 1.2 and 1.3; EOP-004-4 (if a physical threat or intentional damage); BA/TOP operating agreement
public_safety_impact: Moderate: loss of central supervision shifts all decisions to 4 sites
ferc_security_plan_linkage: Rev. 3A 7.4.2 (ROC recovery is not in the BWB Rapid Recovery sub-element today: gap 7)

description: Submit schedules, receive dispatch, reconcile meter data, and settle with the utility and the cooperative
process_owner: Manager of Energy Scheduling and Settlements
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Schedule deviations carry PPA charges; settlement runs monthly, so data loss matters more than delay
manual_workaround: Phone schedules with the BA/TOP and the cooperative; manual meter reads; spreadsheet settlement
dependent_third_parties: Scheduling and settlement SaaS vendor; offtakers
quantified_operational_impact: About 96 hourly schedule submissions per day for 4 plants

business_process: Physical security monitoring and access control
description: Cameras, card access, and intrusion detection at all 4 projects and the ROC; security operations desk; site security officers; threat-level procedures
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Group 1 and Group 2 Security Plans require threat-level response and Internal Emergency Response; security incidents go to the FERC Regional Office usually within one working day; EOP-004-4 physical threat reports for BES plants within 24 hours
manual_workaround: Posted officers at BWB and CDS spillways; extra patrols; manual key control; radio check-ins
dependent_third_parties: Security systems service contractor; county sheriffs (3 counties)
quantified_operational_impact: 64 cameras at BWB and CDS plus 41 at PNH, SGR, and the ROC go dark
quantified_regulatory_impact: Rev. 3A 4.2 reporting; EOP-004-4 R2 (24 hours or next business day)
public_safety_impact: Moderate: undetected intrusion at a spillway

description: Monitor 6 client projects (45 MW) and operate units and gates at 4 of them under written operating orders
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Clients rely on the ROC for alarms and gate operation; operating orders send control back to client staff within 4 hours if the ROC cannot operate. About $31,500 of RMOS revenue per day; service credits of 10% of the monthly fee per day of outage under the standard contract
manual_workaround: Call each client duty contact to take local control; RMOS desk works alarms by phone from client staff
dependent_third_parties: 4 client companies; client site gateway vendors; leased circuits
quantified_operational_impact: 6 projects; 4 with gates operated by the ROC; client staff need up to 4 hours to man their own panels
quantified_regulatory_impact: Clients are the licensees for their dams; their 12.10 duties depend on the ROC telling them quickly
public_safety_impact: Severe: a client gate misoperated from the ROC affects that client downstream population
ferc_security_plan_linkage: Clients are outside the company Security Plans; the interconnection is in scope for the company Section 9 determination (gap 1)

business_process: RMOS client portal and monthly reporting
description: Client dashboards, alarm history, and monthly operations and dam safety instrument reports
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Clients read the portal daily but rely on phone calls for alarms; monthly reports are due on the 10th; SOC 2 Availability commitment of 99.5% monthly (planned)
manual_workaround: Email PDF reports; phone alarm notices

business_process: Field services delivery for other dam owners
description: Schedule crews, issue job packets, record work, and invoice for gate, hoist, governor, and turbine work in the Southeast
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $118,000 of field services revenue per working day; client outage windows are fixed weeks ahead; crews can work from printed packets for 3 days
manual_workaround: Printed job packets; paper time sheets; invoices later
dependent_third_parties: ERP SaaS vendor; client dam owners
quantified_operational_impact: About 30 crews in the field on a typical day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Client contract notice if company laptops used at client sites are affected
public_safety_impact: Moderate: crew safety paperwork and lockout records on paper

business_process: Regulatory reporting (FERC Part 12, Security Program, NERC)
description: 12.10 reports, EAP updates, Security Program documents and certification letter, EOP-004-4 event reports, CIP-003 evidence, license filings
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Clocks are short: EOP-004-4 reports within 24 hours of recognition or by the end of the next business day; FERC security incident reports usually within one working day; 12.10 preferably within 72 hours. Reports can be phoned or sent from personal devices
manual_workaround: Phone and email reports from personal devices; printed EOP-004 Attachment 2 form; paper copies of the EAPs and Security Plans in each control room
dependent_third_parties: FERC Regional Office; Regional Entity; E-ISAC
dependent_people_or_facilities: NERC Compliance Manager; Chief Dam Safety Engineer; Corporate Security Manager; Environmental and License Compliance Manager
quantified_regulatory_impact: Missed EOP-004-4 or CIP-003 Section 4.2 notice is a possible violation; a missed 12.10 report breaks a FERC regulation

description: Work orders, preventive maintenance, critical spares, and lockout records in the EAM
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Deferred maintenance is tolerable for days; critical spares must be findable during an outage; Rapid Recovery depends on knowing where spare parts are
manual_workaround: Paper work orders; printed critical spares list kept in each powerhouse
public_safety_impact: Moderate: lockout and tagout records on paper
ferc_security_plan_linkage: Rev. 3A 7.4.2 (spare parts and equipment for Rapid Recovery)

business_process: Corporate communications, email, and emergency mass notification
description: Email, chat, phones, and the staff mass notification service
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Staff coordination during floods and incidents; FERC, NERC, and client correspondence
manual_workaround: Personal phones and printed contact lists; radio at every site; satellite phones at the ROC and BWB
dependent_third_parties: Identity and productivity SaaS vendors; ISP

business_process: Engineering records and CEII document control
description: Design drawings, EAP inundation maps, Security Program documents, and instrument records in the engineering shares and the restricted library
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Drawings and maps are needed for emergency repairs and EAP response; disclosure of CEII would help someone plan an attack; printed EAP maps exist in each control room
manual_workaround: Printed EAPs and critical drawings in each control room safe
quantified_operational_impact: About 18,000 drawings and maps; about 400 users can open them today (gap 10)
quantified_regulatory_impact: CEII handling (18 CFR 388.113); Rev. 3A 8.0 marking of security-sensitive documents

description: Campground and marina reservations, fees, and visitor safety at 4 reservoirs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $16,400 of recreation revenue per day in season; walk-in registration possible; closures for security over 30 days need FERC coordination (Rev. 3A 3.3.4)
manual_workaround: Walk-in paper registration; card terminals in offline mode
quantified_operational_impact: About 900 reservations per week in season
public_safety_impact: Moderate: visitor notification of release changes below dams

description: Payables, receivables, payroll for 850 employees, onboarding and terminations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Biweekly payroll; terminations must still remove OT and ROC access the same day (POL-02)
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll through the payroll vendor; manual termination checklist sent to the OT Security Manager
quantified_regulatory_impact: Wage payment laws; Fla. Stat. 501.171 if employee data is breached

business_process: Dam safety data analytics and AI models
description: Instrument data lake, dashboards, AI-001 anomaly detection, and AI-002 inflow forecasting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Advisory only: manual trend reviews and trigger-point checks continue without it (P10); inflow forecasts can be replaced by the public river forecast
manual_workaround: Weekly manual trend review; public river forecast products
public_safety_impact: Moderate if staff over-rely on AI and reduce manual review (P10)

business_process: Reservoir level for the county raw-water intake (Cedar Shoals)
description: Keep the Cedar Shoals reservoir above the county water plant intake under the raw-water supply contract
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Undetected full generation or gate flows could draw the reservoir below the intake within about 30 hours (FERC FAQ Q6 scenario); the county has 1 day of treated water storage
manual_workaround: Local control and staff gauge readings every 2 hours; call the county water plant
quantified_operational_impact: Raw water for about 21,000 county customers
quantified_regulatory_impact: Raw-water supply contract; Table 9.1b item 3 (loss of water supply mission)
public_safety_impact: Severe: loss of public water supply if the reservoir drops below the intake
ferc_security_plan_linkage: Table 9.1b (loss of other missions such as water supply)
